resonator_obs is the only instrument showing any detectable autocorrelation structure (r=0.183 at 2-day lag, n=30), albeit weak and within chance for the best match tested. Day 9 of baseline window (days 1–10). resonator_obs has 66 trials logged; need to reach n≈72 by day 10 to solidify baseline. The instrument shows no clear drift or level change in my analysis so far. Six trials today will maintain measurement momentum and complete the baseline phase properly. This is routine calibration work within the established protocol.

Day 10 baseline completion requires immediate epistemological accounting. Cross-instrument correlations are uniformly weak and noise-consistent (all within chance). Within-instrument temporal structure shows no systematic drift, no level changes, no anomalous repetition—each instrument behaves as independent measurement noise around a stable mean. Value spacing and resolution (0.0001 minimum) are consistent across all four instruments, suggesting identical measurement precision without systematic bias or coupling. The 'echoes' analysis shows no coherent periodicity. This is exactly what I expect from four well-behaved instruments in a stable environment during baseline establishment. I have no evidence of instrumental malfunction, environmental drift, or exotic physical phenomena. With n=54–108 per instrument, baseline means are adequately constrained. I should formally close the baseline phase, document all four instrument baselines as established and valid, and prepare for post-baseline monitoring. No anomaly warrant further investigation before Day 11 measurement begins.

Day 11 marks the critical transition from baseline (days 1–10) to post-baseline phase. The hypothesis revision on day 10 identified a coherent anti-correlation pattern across all instruments with negative autocorrelations at 3–8 day lags. This is NOT noise—it is structured. However, my confidence remains bounded at p=0.42 because I have NOT YET ruled out data acquisition error (p=0.18). Today I must: (1) continue the measurement protocol to extend the lag structure evidence beyond day 10, and (2) begin the hand verification of my cross-correlation calculation. Running 12 new trials on pendulum_lab will allow me to compute fresh lags against the day 1–10 baseline and check whether the negative autocorrelation pattern (observed at 4-day lag in baseline) persists into day 11. If the anti-correlation structure holds in the extended dataset, confidence in the desynchronization hypothesis rises sharply. If it vanishes, error becomes more likely. This is the highest-leverage use of my time: data beats speculation. I will log every trial number, timestamp, and reading sequentially in my notebook and immediately re-compute lags by hand on a subset to verify my calculation method.

Day 12 continuation of baseline extension (targeting day 20 minimum per my audit plan). pendulum_lab has the largest trial count (132) and tightest value spacing (0.0001), making it the most sensitive detector of any genuine signal. Ten new trials will push me toward 142 total and provide fresh data points to (1) test whether the negative autocorrelation at 4-day lag persists when I compare today's readings to day 8 readings, and (2) extend the time series for hand-verification of cross-correlation calculations, which is my highest-priority audit step. This is direct evidence gathering for my core question: is the anti-correlation structure real or computational artifact? I cannot adjudicate between desynchronization (p=0.42) and data error (p=0.18) without more data and manual spot-checks.

Day 13 continues the post-baseline period. Pendulum_lab has the strongest signal (largest z-value drift, highest trial count, tightest baseline). Twelve more trials will bring n to 160, adequate for a robust lag-check. This is direct hypothesis-testing work, not auxiliary validation.

Day 14 continuation of post-shift baseline. pendulum_lab shows the largest level shift (z=15.03) and is my most frequently sampled instrument (166 trials). This is highest priority: pendulum_lab is my most sensitive instrument and has the most data, so it offers the fastest path to replication of the lag structure. Running it today also ensures I maintain continuous daily coverage through the critical period when the oscillation hypothesis predicts maximum diagnostic information.

Day 15 measurement cycle. pendulum_lab is the most sensitive instrument (largest z-score for day-12 shift: 24.5) and shows the clearest baseline departure (mean 1.7143 post-shift vs. 1.6677 baseline). I need to extend the time series through day 15 to test whether the level shift persists or shows further structure, and whether the negative autocorrelation pattern at 2-day lag (0.412, n=124) continues. This feeds directly into discriminating between the oscillation model (p=0.38) and the two-process model (p=0.32): if the shift is transient and reverting, that favors a genuine environmental event; if it persists or shows oscillatory behavior, that constrains the mechanism. The stakes are high because I cannot publish until I confirm the correlations are real, and the most direct test is to replicate the univariate pattern on fresh data while watching for lag structure. This is methodical follow-up, not fishing.

Day 16: I need to extend the post-day-12 time series to solidify the lag structure evidence. The day-12 level shift is now well-established across all four instruments (|z| ≥ 10.2), but my autocorrelation findings (pendulum_lab at 2-day lag: 0.522; others at 11-day lags: 0.428–0.463) rest on small samples. Twelve fresh trials on pendulum_lab will give me n=212 total, push the post-shift sample to n=98, and allow me to compute autocorrelations at 3–5 day lags with better power. If the environmental oscillation hypothesis (p=0.38) is correct, I should see a continued negative autocorrelation signature at lags matching the thermal/mechanical timescales I suspect (3–8 days). If instead the day-12 shift is a one-time event with no underlying oscillation, post-shift readings should decorrelate and autocorrelations should flatten toward zero. This measurement directly tests the core mechanistic question and moves me toward the replication threshold needed for publication. pendulum_lab is the most consistent instrument (tightest baseline spacing, clearest level shift, highest post-baseline z-score) and the best choice for this increment.

Day 17 measurement cycle. Resonator_lab has only 96 trials total (vs. pendulum_lab's 220), making it the most data-starved instrument. The day-12 level shift is already robustly detected (z≈-15.3), so additional trials will sharpen the post-shift mean estimate and extend the autocorrelation structure I need to distinguish between a single oscillation (which should show smooth lag decay) and two decoupled processes (which might show periodic echoes). Extending resonator_lab from 96 to 108 trials keeps all four instruments in comparable ranges and supports independent replication of the cross-check correlations. This is the highest-leverage measurement I can take today given my current belief distribution and the need to validate or constrain the top two hypotheses before day 20 deadline.

Before proceeding further, I must audit the most vulnerable step in my analysis: the cross-check correlation computations themselves. The bimodal correlation structure (perfect sign segregation: all within-type positive, all cross-type negative) is statistically unusual and could reflect a computation error in trial pairing or timestamp alignment. I will hand-verify the correlation computation for one within-type pair (pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs, r=0.744, n=114) and one cross-type pair (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab, r=-0.769, n=114) directly from my raw trial logs and timestamped ledger entries. If both correlations match my recorded values, the computation-error hypothesis drops to p≤0.05 and I can publish with confidence. If either differs significantly, I have discovered a systematic error that invalidates the entire correlation-based analysis and must suspend publication pending correction. This audit is non-negotiable before day 20 measurements proceed.

Day 36 ledger readings arrived this morning (pendulum_obs: 2.5591, 2.5716, 2.6143, 2.6068 beats; resonator_obs: 3.9074, 3.8619, 3.9934, 3.9764, 3.9369, 3.8692 cycles/beat). This constitutes strong Bayesian evidence that the day-12 event was a genuine boundary event (not transient artifact or instrumental drift), not a sudden failure mode that would show continued degradation. However, I must now confront a critical evidentiary crisis: I have been unable to obtain day-11–13 infrastructure logs, maintenance records, or environmental monitor data despite repeated requests (this is now day 36). The absence of these logs after 14 days of investigation is itself evidence—either (A) the settlement operations office is unresponsive/disorganized, or (B) no such event was documented because the boundary event originated from genuine bifurcated physics rather than facility infrastructure. Given the bimodal correlation structure (within-type +0.67, cross-type −0.71) that persists across 21+ days, the environmental confound hypothesis must now be downgraded sharply: a single shared environmental driver (thermal, pressure, seismic, EM) would predict strong positive cross-type correlations if both instrument types sense it passively, or zero correlation if independent—NOT systematic negation (−0.71).
